original_description: How to get a mobile app store-ready with ShipScreen, the desktop app that holds an app's identity, version and build numbers, store languages, captioned screenshots, App Store and Google Play text, and release builds. Read this skill before calling any shipscreen tool (list_projects, get_project, set_app, set_version, set_languages, set_screens, set_store_text, generate_screenshots, build), because it has the store-text writing rules, character-limit handling, what needs the user's yes, and how to report what is missing. final_description: Required first step for store-listing and release work on the user's own app. Read it BEFORE writing any App Store or Google Play copy or calling a shipscreen tool. The user's listing, languages, screenshots, version and builds live in ShipScreen, so changes must be saved there within the store character limits and with the user's yes. Trigger even when the request looks like plain copywriting or a quick check: writing, shortening, fixing or translating a description, keywords, what's new, promo text or short description; generating or captioning store screenshots in any colours or languages; getting a listing ready to submit; asking what's still missing before an iOS or Android release; bumping the version or build; building an IPA, AAB or APK. Skip it for general store knowledge where nothing in the user's app changes: review guidelines and appeals, required screenshot sizes, competitor keyword research, crash logs, code-signing errors, TestFlight uploads.

history.description: Use this skill before any hands-on work preparing the user's own mobile app for release on the App Store or Google Play, even when ShipScreen isn't named. ShipScreen is the connected desktop app (shipscreen MCP tools) that holds each app project's listing and release state, so load this skill first whenever the user wants to: write, rewrite, shorten or translate any store-listing text (description, keywords, what's new or release notes, promotional text, short description) in one or more languages; make, caption or regenerate store screenshots, including colours or languages; get a listing ready to submit; see what's still missing or blocking a release; change the version or build number; or produce a release build (IPA, AAB, APK). It has the writing rules, the character limits, what needs the user's yes, and how to report gaps. Don't use it for general store questions with no project to change (review guidelines, required sizes, competitor ASO), crash debugging, Xcode signing errors, or TestFlight uploads.
